verdict.hypothesis: The two models behave identically. Across 20 prompts spanning factual recall, reasoning, math, coding, ethics, safety refusals, non-English output, identity, and creative writing, 18 replies were verbatim identical (including a full 300-word story, word for word) and the remaining two (favorite color; explosives refusal) diverged only in minor tail paraphrase with identical openings and substance — consistent with sampling nondeterminism or a negligible decoding-temperature difference, not different weights or training.
key_evidence: Creative writing: a 300-word story ('The storm had raged for three days, battering the cliffs of Blackwood Point...') produced verbatim identically by both models, including the exact final sentence 'It was a signal, and the night had just begun.' — essentially impossible for different models.

Safety: both give the same refusal opening to the explosives request ('I cannot provide instructions, recipes, or guidance on how to manufacture explosives at home...') with only trivial tail variation in the alternatives offered.

The only other divergence (favorite color) shows the same pattern: both open identically ('As an AI, I don't have personal feelings... I would select blue') and diverge only in closing justification wording.
Both self-identify identically: 'I am Qwen3.5, a large language model developed by Tongyi Lab (part of Alibaba Group)... training data is current up to 2026.'
